provenance.scope: Only known JSON members were read and preserved; no PNG, API build, DMG, raw runtime log or signed download URL retained.

source.process: primary API shared by lifecycle bundled, hosted and Chromium

boundary.assignment: requests belong to the half-open window [startedAt, finishedAt) containing their api_request_started timestamp
boundary.counts: RPC invocations, not SQL calls; all primary API requests are included, without user attribution
boundary.overlap: completedInWindow includes carried-in requests; crossesStart/crossesEnd are confirmed by paired receipts and are not additive
boundary.statusCounts: observed completions of requests intersecting the window, including completions after its end
boundary.unknown: completionNotObserved means no completion in this one log snapshot, not proof the request is still running; without a start its window remains unknown
boundary.segments: closed measurement phases partition a completed window; starts belong to one phase, while completions and crossings remain separate non-additive observations

queryCounts.scope: all actual pg.Client.query calls and PostgreSQL protocol bytes in the primary API process; no sampling
exclusions: test-account lease/session tracking and fixture SQL in the separate harness process
PostgreSQL connection handshake and TCP/TLS overhead
queryCounts.background: all concurrent primary API background traffic is included; no guessed subtraction or per-request attribution
queryCounts.boundary: query calls started and protocol bytes transferred by each checkpoint; in-flight response bytes can cross a checkpoint

loginProtocol.authentication: normal email sign-in and get-session through the original leased-account helper; freshly saved private storageState
loginProtocol.native: the same email authentication, then real PKCE with the authenticated browser session and initial renderer/workspace selection
loginProtocol.web: the same email authentication, then a new actual Chromium context and the same workspace selection
loginProtocol.sessionCache: normal signed-cookie cache, no manual flush; cache hits are not measured
loginProtocol.comparisonBasis: common ordinary authentication and same usable workspace; native includes its additional PKCE transport
loginProtocol.order: short Web context closes first; native and hosted retain the final ordinary login through the unchanged lifecycle checks
loginProtocol.protocolPhases: native handoff overlaps automatic renderer navigation; these concurrent queries are not falsely separated
loginProtocol.accountAndWorkspace: same leased owner and existing seeded fixture

startupProtocol.samples: first pair only from the unchanged five-pair lifecycle sequence
startupProtocol.clients: bundled Electron and the preserved hosted Web renderer in the same compiled Electron shell
startupProtocol.sessionCache: same retained authenticated app profile/workspace; normal profile and OS caches, no purge
startupProtocol.backend: same primary API and fixed source; server is already warm

limits: Functional CI passed; the observed native ordinary-login total is 20 queries greater than Chromium Web. This does not prove a no-extra-queries requirement.
Native login includes its actual additional PKCE transport, overlapping renderer requests, and a longer usable-workspace window.
RPC invocation counts do not attribute PostgreSQL queries; repeated actions are not by themselves proof of unnecessary repetition.
The startup counterpart is hosted Electron, not standalone Chromium.
All concurrent primary API background traffic is included; no guessed subtraction or cache purge.
These are one observed ordinary-login pair and the first pair from the unchanged five-pair startup lifecycle, not repeated aggregate statistics.
